newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures end higher on weaker yen.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures end higher on weaker yen.

text.p: All Tokyo gold futures closed higher on Friday, as the yen's weaker tone against the dollar during the afternoon session encouraged individual investors to buy, but the volume was thin, traders said.
The yen-based gold futures were five to 14 yen per gram higher at the close, with the most-active December 1997 up eight yen at 1,322 yen per gram.

Spot gold was quoted at $354.40/354.90 per ounce at 0720 GMT, against $354.10/354.60 in New York on Thursday. Some Japanese trade houses bought on the spot market in the late afternoon, selling in the Tokyo futures, traders said.
"Some traders in Hong Kong and Singapore also had light buying in the afternoon," a major trade house official said.
Spot gold is expected to move between $350 and $355 per ounce next week, local traders said. "I think producer selling will emerge when gold prices gain to around $355," another trader said.

Tokyo platinum futures ended four to nine yen higher, with the benchmark December up seven yen at 1,343 yen per gram. The weaker yen supported the market in line with gold, traders said. "The yen/dollar rate and gold market currently determines Tokyo platinum futures," a brokerage house trader said.
December palladium futures ended up four yen at 455 yen per gram and silver futures were up 1.5 yen at 179.2 yen per 10 grams.
